messages:
anya: Quick post-all-hands note about a specific regression pattern we saw in staging: mixed traffic (many tiny chat pings + occasional long completions) created a 'funnel' where microbatching delayed tiny requests. Two asks: 1) short mitigation checklist, 2) recommended default routing/policy for mixed traffic.

samir: Good catch. Mitigations: a) split pools by request profile (tiny vs long), b) enforce per-request latency cap so tiny requests bypass batching, c) reduce microbatch_window_ms for mixed workloads. We'll add a short RFC to the repo.

leo: From perf runs: for mixed traffic try 
- microbatch_window_ms=3
- max_batch_size=5
- enable request_priority=true (tiny requests marked high)
- prefix cache enabled for common prompts
Also consider token-prefetching for long completions to avoid head-of-line blocking.

anya: Nice. Harper, can ops support a canary that routes 10% of traffic through a 'latency-first' policy so we can measure impact?

harper: Yes. Can spin up a latency-first pool and route 10% for 24h. Ops checklist: pin canary nodes, disable scale, enable 100% trace sampling, collect microbatch_delay histograms, KV hit ratio, and per-profile latency. Abort conditions: sustained p50 increase >25% vs baseline for latency-first pool or p95 > 2x baseline.

diana: For the canary telemetry, please include span attrs: batch_profile, request_size, priority. We'll need to correlate microbatch delay with GPU utilization spikes. Also add an alert if head-of-line blocking rate > 1% (we have a small detector).

leo: Short sample routing config to paste: 
```yaml
routing:
  policies:
    - name: latency-first
      match: request_size<=4
      pool: low-latency
      batching: disabled
    - name: balanced
      match: default
      pool: default
      batching:
        microbatch_window_ms: 3
        max_batch_size: 5
```

anya: Perfect. One operational question: how does kv_prewarm interact with latency-first pool? Does it help tiny requests?

leo: kv_prewarm mainly benefits longer multi-token completions by warming KV entries; for tiny single-token requests it has minimal effect. Latency-first wins by avoiding batching and routing to warm nodes. Use kv_prewarm on balanced pool if memory allows.

harper: I'll schedule the 10% canary for tomorrow. Ops will collect traces and push a short dashboard with p50/p95 for both pools, microbatch_delay, KV hit ratio, and H-O-L detector.

ops-bot: canary deploy scheduled -> job #8422 (latency-first experiment). Estimated start 07:10 UTC.

anya: Great, thanks everyone. I'll collate this into a one-page runbook and post the link once ops has the dashboard. If kernel team has an automated priority header we can use, please drop it here.
